prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: side impact at intersection in Houston, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported shoulder injury. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1396; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was traveling northbound in the left lane approaching an signalized intersection in Houston, Texas, when the vehicle was struck on the driver's side by Driver 2, who was proceeding westbound and entered the intersection as the light changed. Officers arrived to find both vehicles stopped in the roadway with visible crush damage to the driver's door panel and the front quarter panel of Driver 1's vehicle, damage consistent with the angle and force of a side impact of this type. Driver 2 stated the collision occurred just as described by Driver 1, and two independent witnesses at the corner gave statements that matched this account. Photographs taken at the scene show the positions of both vehicles and the damage to each. Driver 1 was seen and identified at the scene by officers and by the witnesses as present in the driver's seat at the time of impact, and Driver 1 reported pain in the right shoulder, an injury officers considered plausible given how the vehicle was struck. No prior damage to the vehicle was noted in the records checked. Passenger, seated in the rear, reported no injury and was transported by a separate vehicle. Driver 1 is listed as a named driver on the policy covering the vehicle.
